title: Model Rollout and Versioning Standard
author: Maya Srinivasan
body:
h1. Objective
Define Redwood Inference requirements for model versioning and production rollouts across serving routes. This standard exists to ensure rollouts are reversible, observable, and safe under partial failures.

h1. Version identifiers
A model version MUST be uniquely addressable and immutable once marked ready for production. Version IDs must include:
* model family name
* architecture variant (if applicable)
* build date or build hash
* quantization profile (if not default)

Example: rw/mistral-large:2025-09-22-q8_0

h1. Registry states
Every model version MUST move through these states:
* onboarding
* staging_ready
* ready_for_prod
* stable (production default)
* deprecated

The registry record MUST include a clear owner and a changelog summary suitable for oncall triage.

h1. Routing policy requirements
For each production route, the routing policy MUST define:
* primary target (stable)
* fallback target (last-known-good)
* traffic split weights
* region behavior (if multi-region)
* safety constraints (e.g., disallow cross-family fallback unless explicitly approved)

h2. Fallback compatibility
Fallback MUST be compatible at the API contract level:
* same response schema
* same tool/function calling support on the route
* compatible tokenization behavior for billing (no negative billing drift)

If compatibility is uncertain, the rollout MUST be blocked until a safe fallback is defined.

h1. Rollout principles
Rollouts MUST:
1) Start with a canary on production traffic
2) Have explicit, pre-defined gates (SLO + saturation + correctness)
3) Be reversible within minutes
4) Update the last-known-good pointer only after stability is demonstrated

h1. Required artifacts for any Hosted API rollout
* Rollout runbook followed (driver recorded)
* SLO gates adhered to (no ad-hoc weakening without SRE approval)
* Monitoring coverage for the route and version
* Rollback plan and rollback owner
* Customer communications plan if customer-visible

h1. When to require additional review
Extra review is REQUIRED for any of the following:
* introducing a new model family to an existing route
* enabling a new feature flag on the route (e.g., structured output mode changes)
* changing tokenizer or token accounting logic
* significant batching/caching configuration changes

In these cases, reviewers MUST include one person from eng-serving-runtime and one from eng-sre.

h1. Exceptions
Exceptions are allowed only for emergency mitigations. The driver MUST:
* document the rationale
* list what was skipped
* open a follow-up task to restore compliance within 5 business days.
